bench.reason: baseline 0.008 ms is below the 15 ms noise floor even at the largest bench scene (geo=400 array=20000); measured anyway -- every accept must clear 1.15x on two independent timings

ledger.hypothesis: At bench size the board is k x k (width/height move to k every tick) and is reseeded every tick, so compute() is allocation-bound, not arithmetic-bound: ~20 nd::Array temporaries at 3-4 allocations each (uv from_data, slice/floor/sub/mul chains, random() + cmp_lt, board copies, output from_data) dominate the ~7 us tick. Fusing RandomState.random()<density into one loop over the generator, and computing only the 2*h*w words of the first MT twist that are ever read, removes most of the rest. No cross-evaluation cache was added: the harness seeds reset=1, so seed=int(frame) changes every tick and a seed-keyed RNG-stream cache would miss on every tick (it would only pay off for reset-off reseeds, which the bench never exercises).
ledger.note: confirmed twice (incumbent under the noise floor): 0.004 / 0.006 ms
ledger.risk: Bit-parity of the fused RNG (the partial twist must equal the prefix of the full twist, and draws >= 624 must take the full path) and of the scalar uv->cell math (uv rounds through float exactly once, as the float2 plug does; int64 truncation and min() strictness kept). Checked with a standalone 24k-case comparison against the original nd:: kernels across seeds (incl. masked negatives), shapes (1x1 .. 64x64, 622/624/626 draws), densities (0, 1, out of range), multi-step chains and 20k random uv samples: 0 mismatches. A second round reusing the board buffer in place measured a tie (0.0037 vs 0.0037 ms) and was reverted.
ledger.theme: Replace the nd::Array temporaries on the per-texel path with scalar math and a fused seed/step kernel, so one texel costs a floor, two multiplies and a table lookup instead of ~70 heap allocations.

ledger.hypothesis: the bench moves width/height every tick so every tick reseeds a k x k board (k <= 13, at most 169 cells); the cost is not the grid but the serial 624-step MT19937 init, the twist, and ~5 heap allocs for a fresh nd::Array -- the seed itself repeats (reset off => seed 0), so the tempered doubles are a pure function of one input that holds, and memoising them plus reusing the board's bit-vector, shape and stride storage removes almost all node-side work; a prefix-twisted generator is marked partial and rebuilt from the seed if a later same-seed board needs more draws, so hits, misses and extensions all reproduce the fresh stream bit-for-bit (checked standalone: 12001 boards, 0 mismatches; in-place Conway step: 5000 steps, 0 mismatches)
ledger.note: incumbent under the noise floor: second measurement 0.006 ms did not confirm 0.004 ms
ledger.risk: the cache is keyed on the seed value alone and holds up to 4M doubles (32 MB) per instance -- larger boards stream and bypass it; the node is now within noise of the harness's ~0.003 ms single-texel floor, so further node-side work is unmeasurable here; the in-place step is not exercised by the benchmark (shape moves every tick) and relies on the standalone check plus the parity pass
ledger.theme: cache the RandomState(seed) draw stream per instance so a reseed costs one compare per cell instead of a 624-word MT19937 init and twist, and rewrite the board in place instead of reallocating it

stop_reason: round 2 not-faster -- nothing new to compound from
